Next he examined the white, round stones. He asked, “What shall we do with these stones?” I said, “What do I know, sir?” He asked, “Can you think of nothing to do with them?”[a]

2. I said, “Sir, I do not have this skill. I am no stonecutter. I cannot understand.” He said, “Do you not see how round they are? To make them square, I would have to cut away a lot. But some must be put into the building.”

3. I said, “Then, sir, why trouble yourself? If it is necessary, choose whichever ones you want and fit them into the building.” He chose the larger, bright stones and cut them. The virgins lifted them and fitted them into the outside parts of the building.

4. The leftover stones were carried back to the field they came from and set aside. They were not rejected. He said, “The tower still needs a little more building. Its master certainly wants these stones fitted into the building, because they are very bright.”[b]

5. Twelve very beautiful women were called. They wore black clothes with belts, had bare shoulders and wore their hair loose.[c] They seemed fierce to me. The shepherd told them to carry the rejected stones back to the mountains they came from.

6. The women were cheerful. They carried away all the stones and put them where they had come from. No stones were left around the tower. The shepherd told me, “Let us walk around the tower and see if it has any defect.” I walked around it with him.

7. The shepherd was very cheerful to see how beautifully the tower was built. Seeing it made me desire its construction. It looked as if it had been built from a single stone, without a single joint in it.[d] The stone looked as if it had been cut from the rock. To me it seemed to be one monolith.

translation:
  text: 'Then he came to examine the white, round stones and said to me, “What shall
    we do with these stones?” “What do I know, sir?” I said. He said to me, “Can you
    think of nothing to do with them?”[a]


    2. “Sir,” I said, “I do not have this skill. I am no stonecutter, and I cannot
    understand.” “Do you not see,” he said, “that they are very round? If I want to
    make them square, much must be cut away. Yet some of them must necessarily be
    put into the building.”


    3. “Then, sir,” I said, “if it is necessary, why trouble yourself? Why not choose
    whichever ones you want for the building and fit them into it?” He chose the larger,
    bright ones and cut them. The virgins lifted them and fitted them into the outside
    parts of the building.


    4. The remaining stones were lifted and set aside in the field from which they
    had been brought. They were not rejected. “The tower still needs a little more
    building,” he said. “The master of the tower certainly wants these stones fitted
    into the building, because they are very bright.”[b]


    5. Twelve women were called. They were very beautiful in appearance, dressed in
    black, with belts around them and their shoulders bare, and with their hair loose.[c]
    These women seemed fierce to me. The shepherd ordered them to lift the stones
    rejected from the building and carry them back to the mountains from which they
    had been brought.


    6. They were cheerful and carried away all the stones, putting them where they
    had been taken from. When all the stones had been carried away and no stone lay
    around the tower any longer, the shepherd said to me, “Let us walk around the
    tower and see whether it has any defect.” I walked around it with him.


    7. When the shepherd saw that the tower was beautifully built, he was very cheerful.
    The tower was built in such a way that seeing it made me desire its construction.
    It was built as if from a single stone, without a single joint in it.[d] The stone
    appeared to have been cut from the rock, for it seemed to me to be one monolith.'

  text: 'Then he came to examine the white, round stones and said to me, “What shall we do with these
    stones?” “What do I know, sir?” I said. He said to me, “Can you think of nothing to do with them?”[a]


    2. “Sir,” I said, “I do not have this skill. I am no stonecutter, and I cannot understand.” “Do you
    not see,” he said, “that they are very round? If I want to make them square, much must be cut away.
    Yet some of them must necessarily be put into the building.”


    3. “Then, sir,” I said, “if it is necessary, why trouble yourself? Why not choose whichever ones you
    want for the building and fit them into it?” He chose the larger, bright ones and cut them. The virgins
    lifted them and fitted them into the outside parts of the building.


    4. The remaining stones were lifted and set aside in the field from which they had been brought. They
    were not rejected. “The tower still needs a little more building,” he said. “The master of the tower
    certainly wants these stones fitted into the building, because they are very bright.”[b]


    5. Twelve women were called. They were very beautiful in appearance, dressed in black, with belts
    around them and their shoulders bare, and with their hair loose.[c] These women seemed fierce to me.
    The shepherd ordered them to lift the stones rejected from the building and carry them back to the
    mountains from which they had been brought.


    6. They were cheerful and carried away all the stones, putting them where they had been taken from.
    When all the stones had been carried away and no stone lay around the tower any longer, the shepherd
    said to me, “Let us walk around the tower and see whether it has any defect.” I walked around it with
    him.


    7. When the shepherd saw that the tower was beautifully built, he was very cheerful. The tower was
    built in such a way that seeing it made me desire its construction. It was built as if from a single
    stone, without a single joint in it.[d] The stone appeared to have been cut from the rock, for it
    seemed to me to be one monolith.'
